rules.sectionReferenceMeaning: Use the accepted Latin Niese registry. XI preserves each registered physical occurrence and labels the two accepted Bellum interpolations separately. XII–XV use explicit Niese milestones and unsuppressed source citation labels. Unavailable registry identities do not create records or imply lost Latin text.
rules.textTransformations: Exclude source num labels, notes, heads, trailers, pre-narrative front matter and the exact XII subscription following its explicit niese-end marker. Retain every other running source character, including anonymous narrative paragraphs and all add/del/unclear/corr/expan content. Trim each paragraph fragment edge; join continuing physical paragraphs with two newlines.
rules.phraseBoundaries: Physical source spans preserve actual Latin order. Separate portions of a canonical section share citationUnitId but acquire no artificial adjacency. Zero-width TEI gaps interrupt tokens and phrases. Literal dot/ellipsis clusters and erased punctuation conservatively block adjacency; marginal dots are not interpreted as proof of an omission. Registry-unavailable identities alone introduce no source lacuna or phrase break.
rules.editorialMarkup: Preserve exact add/del/unclear attributes and UTF-16 spans in editorialMarks; corr/expan/s/ref appear in sourceMarkup. Do not silently correct readings, omit marginal source words, or generate display glyphs.
rules.unknownContent: Require the frozen accepted XML and identity-registry hashes, with CRLF/LF equivalence. A changed source, unresolved boundary, overlapping interval, lost running character or unreviewed empty span stops extraction.
rules.sourceProjectionDefinition: Each original narrative paragraph is exactly restored from finished recordId slices plus excluded labels/notes and reversible edge whitespace. Anonymous paragraphs use an explicit xpath: source locator, never an invented XML id.
rules.offsetDefinition: Audit sourceText, flat and recordText coordinates are Python Unicode characters, end exclusive. Published inline marks, textGaps and phraseBreaks use JavaScript UTF-16 offsets.
rules.tokenCountDefinition: Unicode L/N start and L/M/N continuation, with explicit source gap boundaries interrupting token formation.
rules.readerRoute: /antiquities/?book=11&niese={section}; the two registered Bellum interpolations use their accepted association to XI.312.
